name: RF amplifier
description: An RF amplifier with a vector network analyzer (VNA): gain against frequency, gain flatness and 3 dB bandwidth, input and output return loss, reverse isolation, the stability factors K and mu (can it oscillate?), and optionally the 1 dB compression point from a power sweep. Includes checks to keep the amplifier and the VNA from being overdriven. The VNA is calibrated beforehand by the user.

roles.name: vna
roles.description: The network analyzer (two ports), calibrated with the attenuators that will be in the test

sweep.description: start_hz, stop_hz, points, scale (linear|log), if_bandwidth_hz, power_dbm: the VNA source power, keep it low

device.description: label identifies the amplifier; asset_id is its code in the registry of cables and devices

input_attenuation_db.description: attenuation between the VNA source and the amplifier input (the power at the amplifier is this much lower)

max_input_dbm.description: the largest power the amplifier input can take: the measurement refuses to go above it

passband.description: from_hz and to_hz: where the flatness, the worst return loss and the isolation are taken (the whole sweep by default)

gain_edge_db.description: the band edges are where the gain is this far below its peak (3 by default)

frequencies_of_interest.description: the gain is reported at these frequencies

compression.description: frequency_hz, start_dbm, stop_dbm, step_db, compression_db (1): a power sweep at one frequency to find the compression point

limits.description: pass / fail mask on the gain in dB: {"min": 18} or bands

golden.description: check the result against a golden sample of the project (a good unit of the same kind): name (in the golden/ folder of the project) or run (a run file), and tolerances = {curves: [{trace, view, tolerance}], summary: {figure: tolerance}, min_overlap}

confirm_setup.description: ask, before measuring, to calibrate, connect and check the powers
